title: Sideline Out-of-Bounds Box Set
description: A simple box formation with two screens gives the inbounder a safe, well-timed option and a clear release valve against pressure.

content.objective: Inbound the ball safely against pressure using a simple box formation, timed screens and a clear signal.
content.setup: The inbounder stands on the sideline level with the free-throw line. Four teammates form a box on the blocks and elbows. Four defenders guard the box players.
content.organization: Groups of nine: five on offense, four on defense. Rotate roles every two possessions; extra players wait behind the baseline and rotate in.
instructions: The offense sets the box: two players on the blocks and two on the elbows. The inbounder holds the ball and calls the play by number.
On the call, the two elbow players screen for the two block players, who cut to the ball side and to the top.
The inbounder passes to the first open cutter, using a firm pass with a step.
If nothing is open, the closest player breaks back to the ball as a safety valve before the five-second count ends.
Once the ball is in, play out the possession live.
coachingPoints: Signal early and call loudly so everyone hears the play.
Set screens with feet still and arms tucked; the cutter reads the defender before cutting.
Cut sharply off the screen and show a target hand.
The inbounder stays behind the line and waits for the cutter to be open.
commonMistakes: Passing before a cutter is open, into traffic.
Screeners moving as they set the screen.
Every player cutting to the same side, leaving no safety valve.
content.safety: Keep hands off cutters' bodies, and keep the inbounding space clear of players and equipment.
progressions: Add a second option: the inbounder passes to the safety, and the ball is reversed to the far side.
regressions: Run the set with no defenders until the timing is smooth.
variations: Run the same set from the opposite sideline.
Add a five-second count that the inbounder must beat.
